definition: Statistics uses shorthand notation where a bar over a variable (e.g., x-bar) denotes the arithmetic mean of that variable's distribution, and n denotes the number of elements in the distribution.
core_idea: The mean of a series is computed by summing all its values and dividing by the count of values (n), using subscripts (x1, x2, ... xn) to refer to individual elements of the series.
key_points: A bar over a variable name denotes its arithmetic mean.
n represents the number of elements in a distribution.
Subscripts index individual elements of a series (e.g., x1, x2, ... xn).
When multiple series are in play, n can itself be subscripted (e.g., n_x) for clarity, at the cost of more complex notation.

formulas.name: Arithmetic mean
formulas.formula: x̄ = (Σ x_i, i=1 to n) / n

variables.x\u0304: arithmetic mean of the x distribution
variables.x_i: the i-th individual value in the series
variables.n: number of elements in the distribution
